items.title: llm 0.37
items.snippet: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddi
items.title_ar: إصدار llm 0.37 مع موديلات OpenAI جديدة وأمر لإضافة endpoints
items.summary_ar: أطلق Simon Willison الإصدار llm 0.37 من أداة CLI ومكتبة Python الخاصة بـ LLM، ويتضمن ميزات وإصلاحات تراكمت على مدى شهرين. أضاف الإصدار موديلي gpt-6.1-sol وgpt-6.1-terra، وأمر llm openai endpoint add لتهيئة موديلات تستخدم OpenAI-compatible endpoints. كما صار الموديل الافتراضي gpt-6-luna بسعر نصف الموديل الافتراضي السابق
items.why_ar: يمكنه تجربة الإصدار فوراً عبر CLI وPython library لتقييم الموديلات الجديدة وربط أي endpoint متوافق مع OpenAI.
items.title_en: llm 0.37 adds new OpenAI models and an endpoint command
items.summary_en: Simon Willison released llm 0.37, the CLI tool and Python library for LLM, bundling about two months of features and fixes. It adds gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra models and a command to configure OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The default model is now gpt-6-luna at half the previous default's price.
items.why_en: He can try the release immediately to evaluate new models and connect any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

items.title_en: antirion: Fast Open-Source AI Gateway for Routing and Observing LLM Calls
items.summary_en: antirion is a single-binary AI and LLM gateway with a built-in console. It routes, secures, budgets, and observes LLM calls across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and more. It targets teams managing multiple model providers from one place.
items.why_en: A gateway like this directly addresses cost control, security, and observability for multi-provider LLM infrastructure.

items.title_en: axuse: Accessibility-First MCP Server for Browser and Computer Use
items.summary_en: axuse is an MCP server for browser and computer use that works across several agent harnesses. It reads the DOM and accessibility tree via CDP instead of relying on screenshot loops. It offers diffed snapshots, stable element refs, and typed errors with zero dependencies.
items.why_en: You can try it immediately with your existing MCP-compatible coding or agent tools to test browser automation.

items.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
items.snippet: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. Moreover, conventional optimization pipelines lack iterative feedback, while existing recursive improvement approaches often rely on self-generated experiences, limiting ability expansion and yielding diminishing returns. To address these challenges, we introduce CUA-Master, a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework. At the system level, an outer world-data-model flywheel continuously incorporates open-world corpus and leverages evolving model weaknesses to guide subsequent data construction and optimization iterations. At the data
items.title_ar: CUA-Master: توسيع computer-use agents عبر تحسينات تكرارية
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة CUA-Master، وهو إطار تحسين تكراري متداخل بحلقتين لتوسيع computer-use agents. تعتمد الحلقة الخارجية على flywheel لبيانات العالم المفتوح وتوجّه توليد البيانات نحو نقاط ضعف الموديل.
items.why_ar: لأن computer-use agents من أهم الاتجاهات في بناء agents تنفذ مهام فعلية، وهو مجال عملك في POCs.
items.title_en: CUA-Master scales computer-use agents via recursive improvement
items.summary_en: The paper presents CUA-Master, a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework for computer-use agents. An outer data flywheel draws on open-world corpora and targets the model's evolving weaknesses.
items.why_en: Computer-use agents are a direct area of interest for building agent POCs, and this paper addresses their data bottleneck.

items.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
items.snippet: Scaling computer-use agents from individual actions to complex software work requires experience that connects decisions to complete outcomes. We present NorthCUA, an integrated system for turbocharging computer-use agents through experience at scale. Its Experience Flywheel supplies diverse executable tasks to the NorthCUA Harness, which sustains long interactions, records decisions, and checks task outcomes. The Flywheel uses these records to curate verified trajectories. For unsolved tasks, recursive self-improvement evolves reusable skills and preserves verified milestones so later attempts build on earlier progress. Staged Learning combines this experience with grounding data from the F
items.title_ar: NorthCUA: تحسين computer-use agents عبر الخبرة على نطاق واسع
items.summary_ar: يقدم التقرير NorthCUA، وهو نظام متكامل يعتمد على Experience Flywheel لتوفير مهام قابلة للتنفيذ وتسجيل القرارات والتحقق من النتائج. يستخدم النظام trajectories موثقة وrecursive self-improvement لتطوير مهارات قابلة لإعادة الاستخدام في المهام غير المحلولة. كما يجمع بين هذه الخبرة وبيانات grounding ضمن Staged Learning.
items.why_ar: يرتبط مباشرة ببناء computer-use agents لأتمتة العمليات البنكية داخل واجهات المستخدم، ويقدم منهجية للتحقق من النتائج.
items.title_en: NorthCUA: Scaling Computer-Use Agents Through Experience
items.summary_en: The NorthCUA technical report describes an integrated system where an Experience Flywheel supplies executable tasks to a harness that records decisions and checks outcomes. Verified trajectories are curated, and recursive self-improvement evolves reusable skills for unsolved tasks. Staged Learning combines this experience with grounding data to improve agent performance.
items.why_en: Its outcome-verified trajectories and reusable skills map well onto automating back-office software workflows in a bank.

items.title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion
items.snippet: Unlike autoregressive (AR) models, diffusion language models (DLMs) permit parallel token updates, flexible generation, and bidirectional attention, but leading systems rely on costly pretraining or full-model fine-tuning. We present Build Your Own DLM (BYOD), a generalizable LoRA-only recipe for parameter-efficient AR-to-DLM conversion. Without architecture-specific tuning, BYOD induces diffusion generation in Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B; to our knowledge, this is the first reported AR-to-DLM conversion of a Mistral model. The adapters comprise 4.1-5.8% of final parameters while every base-model parameter remains frozen; each 25,000-iteration conversion needs at m
items.title_ar: BYOD: تحويل موديلات autoregressive إلى diffusion language model عبر LoRA فقط
items.summary_ar: يقدم البحث BYOD وهي وصفة LoRA-only لتحويل موديلات AR إلى DLM بكفاءة في عدد المعاملات. تنجح الطريقة على Gemma 2 9B وLlama 3.1 8B وQwen2.5 7B وMinistral 8B دون ضبط خاص بكل معمارية. تمثل الـ adapters بين 4.1 و5.8 في المئة من المعاملات النهائية، بينما تبقى أوزان النموذج الأساسي مجمدة.
items.why_ar: لأنه يفتح الباب لتجربة diffusion language models على موديلات open-source قائمة دون fine-tuning كامل مكلف.
items.title_en: BYOD: Converting Autoregressive Models to Diffusion LMs with LoRA Only
items.summary_en: The paper introduces BYOD, a LoRA-only recipe for parameter-efficient conversion of autoregressive models into diffusion language models. It works across Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B without architecture-specific tuning. Adapters are 4.1-5.8% of final parameters while the base model stays frozen.
items.why_en: It offers a cheaper path to experimenting with diffusion generation on existing open-source models in your stack.

items.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
items.snippet: Recent advances in large (vision) language models have enabled computer-use agents that automate digital workflows via fine-grained keyboard and mouse operations. However, such agents remain fragile in long-horizon settings, where errors accumulate and executed actions leave unintended side effects, making the ability to recover from failures critical. Yet, existing remedies remain inadequate: environment resets are infeasible in proprietary settings, action replay is prohibitively expensive over long horizons, and API-based rollback is limited to web environments, leaving model-based recovery largely unexplored. To address this gap, we present ReTrace, a scalable evaluation framework for sy
items.title_ar: ReTrace: تقييم قدرة computer-use agents على التعافي من الأخطاء
items.summary_ar: يقدم البحث ReTrace وهو إطار تقييم قابل للتوسع لدراسة سلوك التعافي لدى computer-use agents. يعالج الباحثون هشاشة هذه الـ agents في المهام الطويلة حيث تتراكم الأخطاء وتترك الإجراءات آثاراً جانبية غير مقصودة. تقترح الدراسة استرجاع الحالة عبر نماذج model-based recovery بدلاً من الاعتماد على environment resets أو action replay المكلف.
items.why_ar: لأن أي agent يعمل على واجهات حقيقية في البنك يحتاج استراتيجية تعافٍ موثوقة قبل الإنتاج.
items.title_en: ReTrace: Evaluating Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary_en: The paper presents ReTrace, a scalable evaluation framework for studying how computer-use agents recover from failures. It highlights that long-horizon errors accumulate and leave unintended side effects. The work explores model-based recovery as an alternative to costly environment resets and action replay.
items.why_en: Reliable recovery is a prerequisite for deploying computer-use agents on internal banking workflows.

items.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
items.snippet: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that replac
items.title_ar: TinyAstral: نقل harness ذاتي التطور إلى وكلاء صغيرة
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة TinyAstral، وهي طريقة من مرحلتين تحسّن harness لنموذج معلم مفتوح الأوزان عبر recursive self-improvement، ثم تُقطّر معرفته إلى student صغير. كل تعديل على الـ harness يُقبل فقط إذا اجتاز اختباراً إحصائياً مزدوجاً. تهدف النتيجة إلى تقليل inference compute cost مع الحفاظ على قدرة الـ planner على الاسترجاع ومعالجة الأخطاء.
items.why_ar: يهم في تقليل تكلفة inference عبر نماذج أصغر تعمل داخلياً، وهي فكرة قابلة للتطبيق في بيئات بنكية محكومة.
items.title_en: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Small Generalist Agents
items.summary_en: TinyAstral first improves the harness of a frozen open-weight teacher using recursive self-improvement, accepting edits only after a paired statistical test. It then distills trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery into a small student agent. The goal is to retain teacher-level behavior at lower inference compute cost.
items.why_en: Distilling harness improvements into a smaller model is a practical pattern for cutting inference cost in bank-internal agents.

items.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
items.snippet: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. items.title_ar: Library of Layers: ترتيب طبقات transformer ديناميكياً أثناء inference
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة LoL، وهي بنية تعيد ترتيب طبقات transformer ديناميكياً أثناء inference حسب المشكلة المطروحة. تتيح مكتبة طبقات عامة واحدة التنقل بين إعادة استخدام المعاملات وsparsity، أي توازن بين كفاءة المعاملات وكفاءة FLOPs.
items.why_ar: تهم من يعمل على تحسين inference وكفاءة الموديلات المخصصة للبنك.
items.title_en: Library of Layers: runtime reordering of transformer layers
items.summary_en: The paper introduces LoL, an architecture that dynamically orders transformer layers during inference to fit the problem. A single global library of blocks lets it move between parameter reuse and sparsity.
items.why_en: It matters for anyone optimizing inference efficiency and parameter budgets in custom models.

items.title: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Cross-Repository Joint Development for Coding Agents
items.snippet: As coding agents achieve increasingly high success rates on software engineering benchmarks, recent efforts have sought to increase task complexity through longer horizons and more extensive code modifications. However, real-world software development often spans multiple interdependent repositories, introducing additional challenges in dependency reasoning, change propagation, and interface consistency. Rather than further increasing complexity within individual repositories, we introduce CrossSWE, a benchmark for cross-repository joint development comprising 171 real-world instances spanning 165 repositories, 20 technical domains, and 13 programming languages. items.title_ar: CrossSWE: معيار لتقييم coding agents عبر عدة repositories
items.summary_ar: يقدم الباحثون CrossSWE، وهو benchmark لتطوير مشترك عبر repositories متعددة يضم 171 حالة واقعية تغطي 165 repository و13 لغة برمجة. يركز على التحديات مثل dependency reasoning وchange propagation وinterface consistency. الهدف هو قياس قدرة coding agents على العمل خارج حدود repository واحدة.
items.why_ar: يهم مهندساً يبني coding agents أو يقيّم قدراتها على مشاريع متعددة الملفات والخدمات داخل البنك.
items.title_en: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Coding Agents Across Multiple Repositories
items.summary_en: The authors introduce CrossSWE, a benchmark for cross-repository joint development with 171 real-world instances spanning 165 repositories, 20 technical domains, and 13 programming languages. It targets challenges such as dependency reasoning, change propagation, and interface consistency. The goal is to measure coding agents beyond single-repository tasks.
items.why_en: It offers a realistic way to evaluate coding agents on multi-service changes that resemble real banking codebases.
